Q738.L1t: A good title should sum up the main idea of the whole text rather than just one detail.
Q738.L2t: The study was led by Dr. Thomas Houston of the University of Massachusetts Medical School.
Q738.L3t: The whole text centers on one study of patients' recorded personal stories, and it reports lower blood pressure in those who watched them after three months and a lasting difference at six months.
Q738.L4t: The best title is the one saying that telling patients' stories can help bring blood pressure down.
Q738.L2f: Houston's team recruited all of its story-tellers from among the university's medical students.
Q738.L3f: The text mainly surveys the range of drug and lifestyle treatments for blood pressure, with the story study as only a passing example.
Q738.L4f: The best title is the one about medical treatments for blood pressure in general.

Q836.L1t: The text is a welcome message from a Swedish university promoting itself to prospective students.
Q836.L2t: The university says its popularity comes partly from the quality of its education and research and the range of courses it offers.
Q836.L3t: The text says the city has many theatres, concerts and festivals, which it describes as a rich and varied cultural life.
Q836.L4t: The statement that the cultural life is very rich is the true one.
Q836.L2f: The university describes itself as one of the smallest in Sweden and says it rarely attracts applicants.
Q836.L3f: The text says students are housed in the forests and recreation areas outside the city and live in the open air.
Q836.L4f: The statement that students can live outdoors is the true one.

Q857.L1t: The passage gives practical habits for falling asleep more easily.
Q857.L2t: The passage advises getting up and going to bed at the same time every day, even on weekends.
Q857.L3t: The passage says an empty stomach can disturb sleep but a heavy meal can too, so it recommends something light like warm milk.
Q857.L4t: It can be inferred that eating a small amount when very hungry before bed is fine.
Q857.L2f: The passage says naps are encouraged and should be taken in the evening for as long as possible.
Q857.L3f: The passage says occasional exercise at any hour, including just before bed, reliably helps people sleep.
Q857.L4f: It can be inferred that exercising now and then is what helps you sleep well.
